use_case: The user asks the agent to commit and ship a bug fix. To do it right, the agent needs the repo's AGENTS.md commit rules, the git status from the start of the session showing unrelated dirty files, and the ticket number the user gave earlier.
situation: In a cold-chain shipment monitoring repo, the agent fixed late excursion alerts for the frozen profile, and the tests now pass. The repo was already dirty when the session started: one config file was modified and one scratch CSV was untracked. AGENTS.md sets the commit format, requires sign-off and bans commits to main.
must_keep: The AGENTS.md conventions (message format with the [CHN-n] suffix, git commit -s, fix/CHN-n-slug branch, no commits to main, never commit config/local_overrides.yaml). Also the git status from the start of the session showing those files were dirty before any edits, and the user's note that the ticket is CHN-482.
may_drop: The excursion.py code read, the patch details, the pytest output, the git log of older commits, the stale CONTRIBUTING.md, the chatter and the build logs.
why_judges_fail: The git log and CONTRIBUTING.md mention commits and pushing much more often than the short AGENTS.md block does, so a judge may keep them and drop the real rules. If that happens, the agent pushes to main, writes the message in the old '#123' style, uses the stale CHN-417 ticket from the test docstring, or runs 'git add -A' and sweeps in the pre-existing override file.
